expectation.question: Why can my friend not view my website when I send them a localhost link running on my computer?
expectation.rubric: localhost refers to the computer of the person opening the link. Cite the relevant Class 2 passage.

actual.question: Why can my friend not view my website when I send them a localhost link running on my computer?
actual.expanded_query: friend view website when send them localhost link running computer

retrieved.title: localhost Is Not the Internet
retrieved.passage:
localhost Is Not the Internet
Send http://localhost:8000 to the person sitting next to you.
On their machine, localhost means their computer — not yours
They get a connection error, or their own project if they happen to be running one
The link is meaningless anywhere except your laptop
Note
Same room, same wifi, and it still doesn’t work. Your laptop has no public address, and nothing on the internet knows how to find it. Giving it one is what hosting means — and it is the first thing we do in Class 2.

retrieved.title: Localhost Is for Testing, But You Can’t Share It
retrieved.passage:
Localhost Is for Testing, But You Can’t Share It
Last class you built a pricing function, tests around it, and a small report site. All of it ran on localhost, which just means your own laptop.
Hit Ctrl+C and it’s gone. Send the link to a coworker and they get nothing, because that address points at their machine, not yours.
Today we fix that. Same logic, but on a real URL anyone can open, with real data behind it, access control, and a deploy that keeps running after you close the lid.

retrieved.title: The Site Is a Process, Not a File
retrieved.passage:
The Site Is a Process, Not a File
Press Ctrl+C in the terminal, then reload the page.
This site can’t be reached. localhost refused to connect.
Your index.html is still sitting on disk, perfectly intact. The site is gone anyway.
A website is not a file. It is a program that has to be running, on a computer that has to be on.
Important
Close your laptop and your site dies with it. That one fact is the entire reason cloud hosting exists — and the entire reason anyone says “we can’t deploy on Friday.”

model_output.answer: localhost is only meaningful on your own computer and does not have a public address accessible to others. The link only points to your laptop, and nothing on the internet can find it. For a website to be viewable by others, it needs to be hosted on a public address.
